name: What are the biggest hidden costs in a fourplex build?

mainEntity.name: What hidden costs surprise owners when building a fourplex in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What hidden costs surprise owners when building a fourplex in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Owners often budget for framing, finishes, and permits but miss the site-specific costs that can change a fourplex budget quickly. In Los Angeles, those surprises often include utility trenching, sewer capacity upgrades, grading, haul-away, tree removal, demolition, off-site improvements, and plan revisions during review. If the lot has a slope, narrow access, or older infrastructure, the risk rises again. A good answer should explain which items are usually fixed-price and which are not, plus how to build a realistic contingency. Searchers need clear guidance on when to ask for a soils report, civil review, and preliminary utility coordination before design is finalized. That kind of breakdown is much more useful than a generic construction cost estimate.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most common hidden costs are utility upgrades, soils and geotechnical work, stormwater requirements, retaining walls, fire and life-safety upgrades, parking redesign, and change orders. In Los Angeles-area infill projects, these items can add a large amount after the initial budget is set.
